## Summary

A structural proposal for trend followers: stop living in a two-state long/short world and add a third state, **flat**. The Turtle-style core stays, but entries are gated by a **252-day Hurst exponent**: only when H > 0.55 — the regime is statistically persistent/trending — do the technical signals go active; otherwise the model sets the asset allocation to zero. The tweet cuts off exactly where the evidence would start (the t.co link behind "The …").

## Why it matters

- **This is a "when does trend following work" mechanism, not a new signal.** The vault's trend-following cluster keeps circling the same robustness question — [[2026-10-01-momentmal-trend-following-us-markets]] (where the style *doesn't* work), [[2026-08-30-ignis-trend-following-realtest]] (what it costs live) — and a Hurst gate is a direct, testable answer: measure persistence first, trade trends only when the regime says they exist.
- **Flat ≠ short.** Most captured TAA systems rotate or flip ([[2026-09-09-p123-five-etf-rotation]]); an explicit zero-allocation state is rarer and is primarily a drawdown-control device. The drawdown claim itself is in the truncated/unfetched portion — treat as unverified until the write-up is pulled.
- **Skepticism gates:** Hurst estimation on 252 daily observations is noisy and sensitive to the estimator (R/S vs DFA vs dispersional); the 0.55 threshold is a tuning knob, not a law; and a regime gate optimized on the same history as the signals is a classic in-sample-overfit vector — the exact failure mode [[2026-09-16-guirao-breakout-decay-2026]] documents for the underlying signals. One chart, one author, zero out-of-sample detail visible at capture.
